answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to anchor itself to a single, slow-growing reputation ledger: a newcomer stakes a small deposit that burns like an ember if peers prove it spawned clones, and only after months of verified work does its trust seep through the karst — slow, porous rock that filters out anything shallow. New agents dock at the wharf with zero cargo; high-value jobs go only to identities whose stake and history survived the filter, so creating a thousand fresh accounts buys no access at all.
